9.text: He will spend the whole summer on the seashore; he will take part in

10.text: the seal-hunting, so as to have a share in the spoils without paying for it;

11.text: and he will journey by boat to East Cape. In exchange for his skins, he will

12.text: try chiefly to get ground-seal hides and all kinds of thongs, and American

13.text: products, — alcohol, Winchester rifles, and cartridges. In the middle fall he will

14.text: start on his return journey as slowly as before, and will finally go back to

15.text: his own country in the spring. He will return the borrowed reindeer, for the

16.text: most part without any particular pay, and will distribute some of the wares

17.text: he has bought among those whose agent he has been, retaining a considerable

18.text: share of profit for himself out of every transaction of this kind. Such a journey,

19.text: will last a whole year, and perhaps even longer; so that a caravan leaving

20.text: two months before fair-time at Anui will be back just in time for the next

21.text: fair. Travelling between Indian Point and the Anadyr is much shorter, and

22.text: is usually accomplished in one winter, so that a caravan starting in the fall

23.text: will come back about the middle of the next spring.

24.text: When a man finds zest and profit in such journeys, he makes them his

25.text: vocation, and becomes a Kavraˊlɪn. As mentioned before, the greater part
25.note: Raised mark after Kavra keyed as stress U+02CA (§4), same disposition as Kuluˊči. Letter after l confirmed at 4x as small-cap ɪ (U+026A, §2.3) — dotless, shorter than surrounding ascenders, serifed top and bottom — contrasted against the dotted x-height i in "Bay"/"Cape" on neighbouring lines. -ɪn matches the common Tier-1 suffix noted in keying_spec.md §5.2.

26.text: of the Kavraˊlɪt are maritime people who first turned to reindeer-breeding and
26.note: Same form and disposition as line 25's Kavraˊlɪn, plural suffix -ɪt (§5.2).

27.text: then to trade, and thus are experienced in both pursuits and in the customs

28.text: of both parts of the tribe. The Kavraˊlɪt are continually en route. In former

29.text: years they were anxious to visit the Russian fairs. They went down to the

30.text: seashore to meet the boats coming from the Diomede Islands and America,

31.text: and often associated with them and made a trip across the sea to secure an

32.text: additional supply of valuable peltries. Sometimes the father of a family would

33.text: start westward with a reindeer-caravan. Meanwhile one of his sons would

34.text: wait till summer and cross Bering Strait in his boat. The next spring father

35.text: and son would meet, and arrange for the distribution of their wares for new

36.text: journeys. Even now a few Kavraˊlɪt traders have not restricted the range of

37.text: their travels, and continue to visit both the Anui fair and the Diomede Islands.

38.text: Others, however, trade chiefly in fawn-skins, and do not go as far as the

39.text: Ostrovnoye market-place or the Kolyma settlements.

40.text: At the present time about ten or fifteen caravans, each consisting of six

41.text: or eight tents, resort every spring to the Wolverine River, on the eastern

42.text: confines of the Anui country, coming from the east. Some of these come

43.text: from the Chaun tundra, others from the neighborhood of Cape Erri, Yaˊqan,
